translations.text: The height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, the depth of the abyss, and wisdom—who has measured them?
But follow the Lord and do not abandon him, so that your life may be prolonged in your later years.
Do not boast about your father's dishonor, for your father's dishonor brings you no glory. A person is honored through his father's honor, and a mother's dishonor brings disgrace to her child.
It will be remembered in your favor on the day of your distress. As the sun melts frost, so it will melt away your sins.
For the Lord's work is great, and he is praised among the humble and the holy.
Listen to the poor person, and answer him kindly with gentle words.
Wisdom exalts her children and welcomes those who seek her.
Whoever loves her loves his own life, and whoever comes to her will be filled with joy.
Do not show favoritism when it will harm your own soul, and do not let shame cause your downfall.
Do not prevent a speaker from speaking, for his wisdom is known from his words, and his learning from what he says.
Both mercy and punishment come from him; his punishment descends upon the sinner.
Do not covet unjust wealth, for it cannot save you in your time of distress.
Do not be a slanderer, and do not revile others with your tongue. A thief's shame is small, but the disgrace of someone with a double tongue is great.
A pleasant tongue increases friendship, and a pleasant mouth increases the number of friends.
A faithful friend is a remedy for life, and those who fear the Lord will find one.
Do not laugh at a person who is grieving, for there is one who brings sorrow and who brings joy.
Do not cultivate a lie against your neighbor, and do not do this against your friend or companion.
Remember that [?] will not delay. Humble yourself all the more, for the punishment of sinners is worms and fire.
Do not treat harshly your servant who serves you faithfully, or your hired worker who devotes his life to you.

Fear the Lord and honor the one who serves him. Give him the share commanded to you: the firstfruits, the sin offering, the shoulder portions, the sacred sacrifices, and the first portions of the holy things.
Do not disregard the words of the wise, and learn their proverbs, for through them you will find wisdom and serve rulers.
Do not reveal what is in your heart to everyone, lest ruin become your reward.
Do not go astray with another man's wife, lest you fall into her snares.
Do not dance with a female musician, lest she ensnare you with her singing.
Do good to your neighbor as much as you can, and seek advice from the wise.
Let your deliberations be with wise people, and let all your conversation concern the law of God.
A wise king disciplines his subjects, and an understanding ruler establishes order.
As the ruler of a people is, so are his servants; and as the governor of a city is, so do those within it act.
The government of the earth is in God's hands.
Do not insult your neighbor for any wrong he has done, and do not do anything evil by insulting him.
He uprooted them and destroyed them, and erased their memory from the earth.
Do not boast about the beauty of your clothing, and do not exalt yourself in your days of honor, for God's work is wonderful, and his skill is hidden from human beings.
My son, do not multiply your activities, for if you multiply them, you will not have room to act rightly. If you run, you will not escape, and if you pursue righteousness, you will not attain it.
God's grace visits the righteous, and his favor makes the world glad.
For on the day of death it is easy for God, for he repays each person according to his conduct.
On an evil day, prosperity is forgotten, and at a person's end his deeds become known.
Your happiness wounds your enemies, and your adversity drives your friends away.
Your enemy will stand beside you for a time; when you turn around, you will no longer see him, and he will not stay with you.

With his food he will entice you once, and a second and third time he will strip you bare. After this he will turn away and will not listen to you. Even if he sees you, he will laugh at you and shake his head at you.
Take care that he does not mislead you or make a fool of you, and do not bring sorrow into your joy.
Every animal loves its own kind, and every person loves his fellow.
Who can reconcile dogs with wolves, and who can make a poor person friends with a rich person?
My son, provide for yourself as well as you can, and bring an offering to God according to your means.
Every living being wears out like clothing, for the command of the law was established: "You will surely die."
As with the leaves of a tree whose foliage is thick—the earlier leaves fall and later ones sprout—so it is with every generation of flesh and blood: one is born and another dies.
She will give him a crown of (wisdom and) joy and gladness, and he will inherit an everlasting name.
For God hates everything unclean. [?]
He created human beings in the beginning and left them free to do as they wished.
His eyes are on those who fear him, and he knows every deed of human beings.
He did not spare the region where Lot lived, whose people exalted themselves and made life bitter for Lot.
Every act of charity brings mercy, and everyone receives according to his conduct.
God created human beings from the earth, and he will return them to it again.
He made every living creature fear them and gave them dominion over wild animals and birds.
Their sins are not hidden from him, and all their wrongdoings are before God.
Afterward he will return and repay them, and he will bring the punishment for their sins upon their heads.
Return to the Most High, turn away from injustice, and hate everything unclean all the more.
For God's mercy is great, and he shows mercy to those who praise him.
My child, do not bring sorrow into joy, and do not speak harshly when giving anything.
Before you are judged, examine yourself, and you will find mercy in the time of your distress.
Every discerning person finds wisdom, and she makes the person who finds her faithful and reverent.
A fool is restless until he tells the news he has heard, and he writhes like a woman in labor giving birth to a child.
Correct your friend before anger grows. Let wicked anger pass away for the sake of God's law.
There is someone who favors evil without praising it, yet his heart is full of deceit.
A fool's mind is like a broken jar; it cannot retain anything it hears.
Wisdom is like a gold necklace to a discerning person, and like a bracelet on the right hand.
A fool's foot quickly enters a house, but a man who has suffered in every way lowers his face in shame.
Teaching a fool is like gluing broken pottery together, like waking a sleeper from a deep sleep.
Likewise, speaking to a fool is like speaking to someone asleep. When you have finished speaking, he says to you, "What did you say?"
It is better to carry sand, salt, and a weight of iron than to live with a fool.
I am not ashamed to shelter my friend, and I do not hide from his presence.
Do not let gluttony come upon me or lust overpower me, and do not hand me over to evil desire.
My child, do not accustom your mouth to swearing oaths, and do not mention the name of the Holy One when you swear.
So too a woman who leaves her husband and bears an heir by a lover.
Her memory will be cursed, and she will leave a curse to her household. Her curse and disgrace will never end.
I dwelt in the heavens, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud.
Like a vine, I put forth grace, and my blossoms are the fruit of honor (and glory) and wealth.
He reveals wisdom like light, and like the river Gihon in the days of the grape harvest.
It is better to live with lions and wild beasts of the earth than to live with an evil woman.
For it is (a scourge and) humiliation and great disgrace, and also shame, if a wife supports her husband.
An evil woman is a wound to the heart, darkness to the face, and sorrow to the soul. Like a crippled hand and a lame foot is a wife who does not praise her husband.
A strong woman makes her husband happy, and he completes his days in peace.
Whether rich or poor, his heart is content. Let your face always be bright.
A woman's grace makes her husband happy, and her wisdom refreshes his bones.

These three things grieved my heart, and the fourth brought anger upon me: a fighting (and courageous) man when he is in want and [?]; wise men when they go astray; and someone who abandons righteousness and returns to sin—God will bring him down by the sword.
The speech of someone who swears often makes the hair stand on end, and their quarrels deafen the ears.
Protect your friend and be faithful to him. But if you have revealed his secret, do not pursue him (then, and do not follow) behind him.
Her yoke is an iron yoke, and her shackles are bronze.
You have weighed your words on a balance and placed a door and a bolt over your mouth.
Someone who gives charity lends to his neighbor, and someone who has enough at hand carries out his commandment.
Keep your word and be faithful to him, and when you wish, you will find him because of your righteousness.

Until he has borrowed, he kisses your head, lowers his voice, and treats you gently until he takes your money. But when you ask him to repay, he prolongs the time, repays you with bitterness and quarrels instead of your money, and wears out (and lets pass) your time.
Many do not lend because of a friend's unwillingness, and out of fear that they may suffer loss or be hated.
But be patient with the poor, and do not withhold charity from them.
Lose your gold rather than lose your friend and your neighbor, and rather than let it rust in a storehouse and be lost beneath a stone.
Someone who teaches his son makes his enemy jealous and rejoices in his son among his friends.
Even if his father dies, it is as though he has not died, because he has left someone like himself behind.
For after him there remains someone who will take revenge on his enemies and repay his friends.
Teach your son, and he will give you authority, so that you will not be ashamed of his corruption.
If you have been harsh toward him and done wrong, he will turn you back. By what road, then, will you seek him?
A foolish man vainly longs for falsehood, and dreams terrify a fool.
A dream shifts from one thing to another, and shows you each thing in the likeness of its own appearance.
He strengthens your soul and brightens your eyes; he also heals, gives life, and provides abundant blessing.
Do not bring him deceit, for he will not accept it from you.
The prayer of the poor passes through the clouds and does not turn back until it reaches its destination; it does not withdraw until the Lord sees it.
They too will know you as we have known you, for there is no God besides you, Lord.
When you sit at a lavish table, do not open your mouth wide over it, and do not say, “They have set out a great deal on it.”
As lightning flashes before thunder, so favor goes before the face of a modest person.
Whoever fears the law listens to the commandment of the book, and whoever trusts in the Lord will not go astray.
A wise man trusts and rejoices in the Lord’s law, and the Lord will be his support and make him glad.
By the Lord’s command all the days are distinguished, and the times of his festivals are known by his reckoning.
Some among them he blessed and exalted; some among them he made holy and appeared to them; and some among them he cursed, humbled, and cast out according to their deeds.
And with all this, look at the work of the Most High: everything comes in pairs, [?] each with its counterpart.
Every man takes a wife, but one woman may be better than another.
There is a friend who comes close to you when you are happy, but when you are in distress he becomes your enemy.
He tells you, “You have done well,” and brings you something that will destroy your possessions; then, when you are in trouble, he watches you and laughs at you.
Along with all this, pray to the Most High to make your path straight in purity (in righteousness).
Do not be greedy for every dish, and do not crave every food you see.
The Lord created medicines from the earth, and a wise man will not despise them.
Look at what has happened to me, and know that the same will happen to you too: to me today, and to you tomorrow.
The dead person is at rest. Nevertheless, commemorate him, and then stop weeping so that his soul may rest.
All his thought is devoted to plowing his furrows, and his care is to feed grain to his oxen (and he works until he tames his calves).
He shapes clay with his hands and exhausts his strength as he works with his feet. His mind is set on finishing his work, and his care is to [?] his kiln.
The endurance of his name is worth more than a thousand, and even after his death his work endures.
Listen to me, children of the righteous. Sprout and blossom as a flower blossoms in the dew of the wilderness.
Magnify his name and praise him for his glory with a thousand songs and with the harp. Say this when you praise him.
The deeds of every living being are before him, and nothing can hide from the sight of his eyes.
Anger, jealousy, distress, turmoil, fear of death, rage, and strife: when someone lies down in bed, his thoughts disturb his sleep at night.
Killing, bloodshed, devastation, war, famine, anguish of heart, and scourges.
Brothers and helpers are for a day of distress, but almsgiving is better than both at bringing deliverance.
O death, how bitter is the thought of you when you come upon someone who lives securely, prospers in everything, has strength, and is free to enjoy his food!
Someone who conceals his foolishness is better than someone who hides his wisdom.
Shame before father and mother on account of children’s sexual immorality; shame before a ruler and the great for lying.

Do not sin with her daughter, and do not approach her bed. Be ashamed of reproaching your friend after giving him something; be ashamed of spreading something you have heard; be ashamed of revealing your friend’s confidential counsel.
Concerning balances and measures, and concerning your possessions, whether few or many.
And concerning correcting a fool and someone without understanding, and an old man who pursues sexual immorality in his old age. Then you will truly be wise and knowledgeable in the eyes of everyone.
Do not admire anyone for their beauty, and do not go among women.
He established them, one alongside another, for good. Who can have enough of seeing his goodness?
From the moon the sign of festivals is known, a light that comes to an end as it diminishes.
The beauty of its whiteness is astonishing to the eye, and its showers are marvelous to the mind.
By his counsel the deep dries up, and afterward he spreads [?].
How much can we praise him? For he is greater than all his works.
Much that is unseen is greater than this; we have seen only a little of his work.
There are some whom no one remembers, who perished and became as though they had never been created, as though they had never been born; their children likewise shared their fate.
Their children continue to live according to their ordinances. [?]
He made an everlasting covenant with him, so that the waters of the flood would not destroy every living being.

For this reason he established a covenant with him by an oath, so that the nations would be blessed through his offspring, and so that he would multiply them like the sand of the earth, and his offspring would become numerous like the stars, and he would give them an inheritance from sea to sea and from the rivers to the ends of the earth.

It rested upon Jacob, upon his head, and appeared to him in his blessing. He gave it to them as an inheritance, allotted to them their respective inheritances, and divided them among the twelve tribes.
So that they might offer sacrifices to him continually, every morning, day after day.
The Lord saw them, and they did not please him. He destroyed them in his wrath, did an astonishing thing against them, and consumed them in a blazing fire.
So that they might eat the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gave to him and to his descendants.
He was praised when he raised his hands and lowered his spear against their cities.
In the days of Moses, he and Caleb son of Jephunneh acted mercifully toward them. They stood against the enemy, kept the people from sin, and made them stop their wicked grumbling.
Lions were like young goats to him, and bears were like lambs.
He appointed singers before the altar, and the sound of their voices was melodious and sweet.
He brought famine upon them and reduced their numbers in his zeal.
Elijah ascended in a blaze of fire, and Elisha was filled with his (holy) spirit. In his days, angels did not frighten him, and no one hindered him.
Nothing was beyond his power, and even after his death his body prophesied.
Simon, son of [?], the high priest, built the temple during his lifetime and strengthened the temple building in his days.
In his days he built water fountains and reservoirs whose water was as abundant as the sea.
And like the sun shining in the sanctuary of the Most High, and like the radiant splendor of the rainbow.
And like incense in the fire upon a censer, and like a vessel of beaten gold.
When he received the sacrificial meat from the priests’ hands, standing at his place of service, his brothers stood around him, encircling and surrounding him like palm shoots.
Then he came down and raised his hands over the whole assembly of the children of Israel, to give them the Lord’s blessing with his lips, and so that they might glory in his name.
My soul hates two nations, and the third is not a people.
While I was young, before I went astray, I sought wisdom and put her first in my prayer.
Prefer wisdom to vast amounts of gold beyond counting; acquire her for yourselves.
